30 Two parallel metal plates are at electric potentials of +800 V and +1300 V.
Which diagram best represents the electric field between the metal plates?
A
B
+800 V
+1300 V
+800 V
+1300 V
C
D
+800 V
+1300 V
+800 V
+1300 V

hints: Notice the left plate is at $+800\text{ V}$ and the right plate is at $+1300\text{ V}$ - identify which plate is at higher potential.
Recall electric field lines point from high potential to low potential and meet the metal plates at right angles, with evenly spaced parallel lines where the field is uniform.
Compare the four diagrams for arrow direction between the plates and for the edge lines - check whether the top and bottom lines bulge outward beyond the plates or curve inward.
walkthrough: Identify the given potentials: left plate $+800\text{ V}$, right plate $+1300\text{ V}$, so the potential decreases from right to left by $500\text{ V}$.
State the governing rule: electric field points from high potential to low potential, so $E$ must point from the $+1300\text{ V}$ plate toward the $+800\text{ V}$ plate, i.e. to the left.
This eliminates the diagrams with arrows pointing to the right, leaving only the two diagrams with leftward arrows in the central uniform region.
State the shape rule: between parallel plates the central field is uniform, so lines are straight, parallel and equally spaced and perpendicular to the plates.
At the plate edges the field fringes, so the outer lines must bulge outward beyond the gap, not curve inward into the gap.
Only the diagram with leftward arrows and outward-bulging top and bottom lines satisfies both direction and shape. This is option B.

A.explanation: Arrows correctly point from $+1300\text{ V}$ to $+800\text{ V}$, but the edge lines curve inward between the plates instead of bulging outward as fringing should.

B.explanation: Arrows point from higher $+1300\text{ V}$ to lower $+800\text{ V}$, central lines are parallel and uniform, and edge lines bulge outward correctly.

C.explanation: Arrows point from $+800\text{ V}$ to $+1300\text{ V}$, which is from low to high potential, opposite to the direction of $E$.

D.explanation: Arrows point from $+800\text{ V}$ to $+1300\text{ V}$, so the field direction is reversed even though the outward edge fringing shape is shown.
